extracted.intended_audience: BBC journalists, editors and newsroom decision-makers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting, presenting and weighting news and opinion in BBC output, focusing on impartiality (due weight), newsworthiness and core editorial values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust — foundation of relationship with audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat trust as a primary editorial value that underpins decisions about what to cover and how to present it; editorial choices should protect and build audience trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth and Accuracy — rigorous in establishing truth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be rigorous in verifying facts and sources; accuracy is a core test for whether something should be reported and how it should be framed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartiality — due weight to events, opinion, main strands of argument
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate prominence and representation to major strands of argument and evidence rather than offering simple equal time to all views; apply impartiality consistently across output and over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Integrity and Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Integrity and Independence — free of outside interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest and outside influence on editorial decisions; ensure choices are made on journalistic grounds, not commercial, political or other external pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm and Offence
rubrics_metrics.description: Harm and Offence — balance of expression with avoidance of unjustified harm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh public interest and free expression against the risk of causing unjustified harm or offence; take steps to minimise avoidable harm while preserving necessary reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serving the Public Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Serving the Public Interest — accountability and value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise stories that hold power to account, inform citizens and contribute demonstrably to public knowledge and debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat contributors, interviewees and subjects fairly in selection, portrayal and opportunity to respond; avoid misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider individuals' reasonable expectation of privacy when deciding coverage and what personal information to publish; balance privacy against public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply special care when reporting about or involving children, taking account of welfare, consent and privacy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about editorial processes, sources where appropriate, and any mistakes; explain judgements where this will help audience understanding and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take responsibility for editorial decisions, correct errors promptly and be answerable to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due Weight (key concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOT equal weight for all views; proportional to evidence and support; minority views need not get equal prominence to consensus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply proportional weighting to perspectives based on evidence and level of support. Ensure output 'reflects a wide range of subject matter and perspectives across output as a whole and over an appropriate timeframe' and that 'no significant strand of thought is under-represented or omitted.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness — Significance to BBC audiences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose stories that matter to the BBC's audiences; editorial judgement should consider the likely importance to listeners/viewers/readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness — Interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a reasonable segment of the audience will find the story interesting or relevant when deciding coverage and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness — Importance / Informational value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise stories that provide valuable information, context or understanding that audiences need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness — Unusual / Striking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider novelty, rarity or striking elements as factors that increase news value, provided they meet other editorial tests (accuracy, public interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness — Public interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give priority to stories with clear public interest rationale, such as exposing wrongdoing, informing civic debate, or protecting health and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness — Diverse perspectives over time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that across output and an appropriate timeframe a wide range of subject matter and perspectives is represented so no significant strand is consistently neglected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversial Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Wide range of significant views must be given due weight and prominence, particularly during active controversy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During active controversies give significant views appropriate prominence and ensure editorial judgements about weighting are reasonable and carefully reached; document and be able to justify the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of Unjustified Harm (as newsworthiness factor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding what to publish and how, avoid causing unjustified harm; factor this into news selection and presentation alongside public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Trust Impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how coverage will affect trust in the BBC; avoid approaches that would undermine long-term trust even if they might attract short-term attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from Outside Influence (as newsworthiness factor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether stories or sources are subject to external pressure or influence and guard editorial decisions against such interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate Sourcing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are supported by reliable sources and make sourcing clear to audiences where appropriate; lack of adequate sourcing should reduce prominence or delay publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Considerations (as newsworthiness factor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate privacy implications for individuals when selecting and presenting stories; privacy can limit coverage or determine how a story is handled.
